title: Get Modern Vim
summary: Chapter 1 is the book's installation and setup chapter: it frames the choice between Vim 8, Neovim, or running both side by side, and notes that the two editors can share the same configuration files and plugins. Tip 1 shows how to check an installed Vim's version and compiled features, then how to upgrade to Vim 8 on Debian and macOS. Tip 2 installs Neovim, explains the $VIMCONFIG/$VIMDATA convention used throughout the book, and shows how to make Neovim reuse an existing vimrc through init.vim. Tip 3 enables Neovim's Python 3 provider via the pip client, introduces providers and :checkhealth (including clipboard support), and installs neovim-remote.

concepts.name: Neovim's remote plugin architecture (RPC)
concepts.evidence: Neovim’s remote plugin architecture allows you to extend the editor by making remote procedure calls (RPCs) using any programming language.

concepts.name: Required Vim 8 build features
concepts.evidence: You want to make sure that your build has the +job, +channel, +timers, and +packages features enabled.

concepts.name: Contextual instructions with $VIMCONFIG and $VIMDATA
concepts.evidence: Alternatively, you could set the $VIMCONFIG and $VIMDATA variables for your shell.

concepts.name: Neovim's separate configuration and data directories
concepts.evidence: That’s because Neovim uses different directories to store configuration and data, whereas Vim makes no such distinction.

concepts.name: Neovim as a drop-in replacement for Vim
concepts.evidence: Neovim can be used as a drop-in replacement for Vim.

concepts.name: Using $VISUAL so external programs prefer Neovim
concepts.evidence: You could also set the $VISUAL variable to nvim, so that programs that launch a text editor (such as git commit) will use Neovim.

concepts.name: Reusing a Vim runtime configuration in Neovim
concepts.evidence: Neovim can load your Vim runtime configuration files, but first you have to tell it where to find them.

concepts.name: Vim script compatibility and the job-control caveat
concepts.evidence: Most Vim plugins written in Vim script should just work™ in Neovim. The one area where you have to be cautious is with any plugin that uses job control to perform work asynchronously.

concepts.name: Neovim providers
concepts.evidence: Neovim uses providers to implement some features whose behavior may depend on the system and environment, such as clipboard support.

concepts.name: Clipboard support enabled at runtime
concepts.evidence: In Neovim, clipboard support is enabled at runtime.

concepts.name: Python 3 provider via the pip-installed client
concepts.evidence: To enable the Python 3 provider, you need to install the Python client.[14]

concepts.name: neovim-remote (nvr) for remote control of Neovim
concepts.evidence: Neovim-remote[15] by Marco Hinz is a tool that lets you control Neovim processes remotely.

problems.note: Tip number and tip title are glued together with no separator ('Tip 1Installing'); the heading should read 'Tip 1. Installing Vim 8'. The same glued heading occurs at 792 ('Tip 2Switching to Neovim') and 927 ('Tip 3Enabling Python Support in Neovim'), while body references use a separator, e.g. 'Tip 21, Avoiding Nested Neovim Instances' at 1004.

problems.evidence: Neovim is a fork of Vim. Its main goal to make the editor more hackable has been achieved by modernizing the codebase, introducing a new plugin architecture, and sharing responsibility for the codebase with the community.
problems.note: The clause has no finite verb between 'goal' and 'to make': 'Its main goal to make the editor more hackable has been achieved' reads as though a word ('is') was dropped, in the source or during extraction.
